name: Tokyo Robotics Torobo
summary: A wheeled, force-controlled research humanoid with 7-axis dual arms, a 3-axis waist and an omnidirectional base, torque sensors in every arm and waist joint and 7 kg per arm in the worst posture, built for manufacturing, logistics and service tasks.

germany.statusNote: Tokyo Robotics lists the current Torobo as 'Under Development' and takes enquiries by e-mail (info@robotics.tokyo). No German or EU seller or price found.

specs.label: Height
specs.quote: With a height of 1615 mm and a cart width of 590 mm, the size of the robot is close to that of a human.

specs.label: Payload per arm
specs.quote: The payload of one arm is 7 kg at the worst-case holding posture

specs.label: Joint configuration
specs.value: 7-axis dual arms, 3-axis waist, 3-axis neck, 4-axis omnidirectional base
specs.quote: The joint configuration of 7-axis dual arms, 3-axis waist (pitch, pitch, yaw), 3-axis neck (yaw, pitch, roll), and 4-axis undercarriage (omni-directional mobile base)

specs.label: Battery operation time
specs.conditions: built-in battery; can run while charging

specs.label: Software
specs.value: ROS, MoveIt!, Gazebo; MuJoCo and Isaac Sim models
specs.quote: Since it is ROS-compatible, the robot in Gazebo (a simulator for ROS) and the actual robot can be operated using the same program.

capabilities.sdk: ROS (MoveIt!, Gazebo); simulation models for MuJoCo and Isaac Sim
notes: Head, end effector (hand or in-house gripper) and second PC are options.
Torque sensors in all arm and waist joints allow impedance control and safe contact stops.
Tokyo Robotics also shows a bipedal Torobo humanoid prototype in its videos; this record covers the wheeled Torobo.

images.alt: Tokyo Robotics Torobo wheeled humanoid robot

evidence.task: Lab demos with impedance control: hammering a nail, sawing wood, box transport by teleoperation
evidence.note: Demo videos listed on the maker site; the maker says some videos show the older Torobo.

openQuestions: Price, release date of the current version and export terms are not published.
Earlier Torobo versions were supplied to research labs; whether the current one is sold outside Japan is unknown.
